_doc: Six core puzzles. flag = consequence. reachedWhen = condition under which the puzzle counts as 'reached' – at that moment the variant is chosen by seed and frozen in state.puzzleVariants (never re-rolled). auto = flag is set automatically as soon as State.canUnlock() holds. variants[]: id, location, solution (mechanic key used by Puzzles.js), reference = personalised line for the core screen, plus mechanic-specific fields. Puzzles 1–3 have no variants; their mechanics live in the content files (search effects, forum onRead, chat, search actions).

hint: The record belongs to an account with the same id as yours. Identity is verified against the current registry entry.
Legacy records are keyed to the current registry entry. The date you are looking for is not from 2038.
reference: The date on your own profile opened the old door.
You verified yourself with the date they gave you. It worked. That should worry you.

hint: Legacy accounts used a shared passphrase per node. Someone from the same node might still remember it.
Passphrases were issued per node, not per user. Ask the only other user who is still here.
reference: 8471's word opened your door. It was always the same word.
You used their passphrase. It fit. You were on the same node all along.

hint: Unindexed records are re-linked by the search index: first the event that detached them, then the owner id.
The record was detached during the shutdown. The index re-links detached records when the event and then the owner are queried in sequence.
reference: You searched for the shutdown, then for yourself. That's the order it happened in.
The index gave you back what it had detached. Shutdown first. Then you.
You found it through the files, not the archive.
It was in your own storage the whole time. It had only been renamed.
You found it in the corrupted archive, where nobody looks.
You read a damaged record and it was the only one that told the truth.
It was sent to you. You didn't find it – it found you.
You didn't have to look. Someone made sure it reached your inbox.
